# Generated fixtures

`lzw-legacy-witness.tif` matches the two-depth formal legacy profile witness
(change byte 42 from 8 to 1 for bilevel). Its four compressed bytes are
`00 f7 04 04`: Clear, literal 123, EOI in LSB order. `lzw-legacy-full.tif`
is a 124×31 image and uses explicit codes from tests/lzw_legacy.py to fill the dictionary, reference
entries 258 and 4095, and read another literal. Its .pixels file comes from
the independent Python byte-string dictionary. Both are deterministic mutation
seeds and Rust budget/frame regressions.

`logluv-strip.tif`, `logluv-tile.tif`, and `logluv-pages.tif` are generated by
`tests/logluv_fixtures.py` from known packed LogLuv32 words. Their `.pixels`
files use the independent Fraction-based native LogLuv16 reference. Parameters:
`make(w=127,h=5,rows=3,le=False)`, `make(w=17,h=19,tiled=True)`, and
`make(w=17,h=5,pages=2,rows=2)`. The second page has its own `-page1.pixels`
file. These are API/frame regressions and mutation seeds. The unchanged
upstream 166-byte LogLuv image itself is the concrete proof-witness seed.

## Deflate copy boundaries

copy-boundaries.zlib is generated locally by copy-boundaries.py, using the
repository's bit writer and an independent Python byte-string reconstruction.
Python's zlib validates the resulting stream. It starts with bytes 0..255 and
AB, then length-258 matches at distance 258, 125 at distance 256, one at distance
1 crossing the 32 KiB ring boundary, and another at distance 258. The decoded
length is 33,282 bytes. No external fixture or license was imported.

## Deflate distance-two period

`period-two.py` generates `period-two.zlib` using the repository bit writer and
checks the complete result with Python zlib. Three initial literals are followed
by 129 length-258, distance-two matches, yielding 33,285 bytes. The two-byte source
pair straddles the 32 KiB history boundary after 32,769 bytes; odd output/checksum
chunks exercise phase preservation. No external fixture or license was imported.
